name: Edie Sedgwick
label: Dischord
lede: Justin Moyer played bass in El Guapo, then put on a wig and a dress and became Andy Warhol's most famous Superstar. As Edie Sedgwick he sang songs named for Angelina Jolie, Rob Lowe and Ol' Dirty Bastard, and Ian MacKaye produced some of them.

eras.title: Thirteen songs, each named for a movie star
eras.text: Edie Sedgwick began as a duo: Justin Moyer on bass and vocals, Ryan Hicks on drums, both billed as Sedgwicks. The first record put a celebrity in every title, and then Moyer's health stopped the band.

years.h: Two men named Sedgwick start a band about famous people
years.p: [[Justin Moyer|68cb15fd-5c0c-4b60-ad06-935ac0756a4d]], still in [[El Guapo|be23bf0a-67c6-4b2f-ba2a-89d983f5ebdd]], starts Edie Sedgwick with drummer [[Ryan Hicks|82e2e1d5-cc55-47a3-8ffe-1c10c30401fa]], and both take the surname. The real Edie Sedgwick died of a barbiturate overdose in 1971.

years.big: This is the weirdest album I've ever made.
years.p: Moyer's line to the New York Times, as Dischord quotes it, about the debut: thirteen minimal songs titled for "Faye Dunaway," "Winona Ryder," "Tom Cruise," "Meryl Streep" and, last, "Edie Sedgwick." Mud Memory and Dischord put it out together.
years.xp:
Dischord lists the line-up as Moyer on bass and vocals and Hicks on drums. The celebrity-title format would run for the next decade.

Moyer had already made records with El Guapo, so that line is a comparison with his own catalog.

years.h: Epilepsy diagnosis sends Moyer and Hicks on hiatus
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Justin Moyer was diagnosed with epilepsy in 2001, and the duo stopped.

eras.title: A dress, a wig and an iPod
eras.text: Edie Sedgwick returned in 2004 as Moyer alone, in drag, singing over backing tracks on an iPod while electroclash peaked and celebrity culture went fully tabloid.

years.h: The Warhol Superstar is back, and Moyer is wearing her
years.p: In 2004 Moyer begins performing solo in drag as Edie Sedgwick, billed by Dischord as the Superstar's reincarnation. Wikipedia describes it as electroclash with an iPod for a band.
years.xp:
Dischord's bio says Edie "traveled through many dark nights presenting auditory and visual art," armed with a video projector and the occasional backing band. The songs kept their celebrity titles, with Paris Hilton and Angelina Jolie among them, and the show made Moyer a celebrity character singing about other celebrities.

The clip is "Sigourney Weaver," from the early solo years.

years.h: Her Love Is Real... But She Is Not arrives
years.p: The first record of the solo drag era. Dischord carries it in distribution as ed47, under the title Her Love Real... But She Is Not.

eras.title: A band behind her, and then no dress
eras.text: MacKaye produced the third album while Moyer rebuilt the act as a live band with an all-female line-up. By 2012 there were four Dischord releases, a new name, E.D. Sedgwick, and no dress.

years.cap: Things Are Getting Sinister And Sinisterer, Dischord No. 161, on translucent orange vinyl
years.h: Things Are Getting Sinister And Sinisterer · Dischord No. 161
years.p: Ian MacKaye and Moyer produce the third album at Studio 1654. Songs include "Sissy Spacek," "Angelina Jolie," "Rob Lowe," "ODB" and "Bambi_G.W. Bush."

years.cap: Justin Moyer as Edie Sedgwick, November 2008
yt: Live at Gold Leaf Studios, D.C.
years.h: Edie Sedgwick grows a band, and all of it is women
years.p: Wikipedia dates the new line-up to 2008: Moyer out front, Kristina Buddenhagen on bass, Jess Matthews on drums, Carla Elliot on vocals, with [[Basla Andolsun|ca1ce6ba-8758-49b2-b2b0-573e80659fb2]], later of [[Andalusians|a7572df1-aad3-4851-ab0c-6013a5dbbb6d]], among the players.
years.xp:
Dischord's Andalusians bio is the source for Andolsun's time in the band. It doesn't say which years.

The clip is a live set at Gold Leaf Studios in D.C., probably January 2008 by the uploader's own dating.

years.h: Live at the Black Cat, March 29, 2009
yt: Live at the Black Cat, March 29, 2009

years.h: Three songs on a 7-inch, eleven in the download
years.p: Love Gets Lovelier Every Day is Dischord No. 169: a limited 7-inch plus a download of all eleven tracks, including a mix of Van Halen's "Everybody Wants Some" and a song called "Ava Devine."

years.cap: Justin Moyer of Edie Sedgwick, January 2012
years.h: Heat Wave gets remixed by Deerhoof's Greg Saunier and others
years.p: The single comes out via Mud Memory and Dischord, then as a white-label 12-inch (Dischord No. 175.5) remixed by [[Greg Saunier|2ae4e9b4-9e8b-4a98-920d-4f3a881dac96]], Triobelisk (Shelby Cinca of [[Frodus|ea524f94-2e37-414d-a7e9-61ba96472f0a]]) and Philadelphia's Pink Skull.

years.h: Moyer sleeps on a Cleveland floor with a drum throne for a pillow
years.p: Washington City Paper runs Moyer's "Heat Wave: Edie Sedgwick Goes to SXSW" day by day. He is almost 35.
years.xp:
In the day-two entry he wakes on a Pittsburgh couch after five hours of sleep. In Cleveland about 75 people show up, and most of them watch the Cavaliers beat the Thunder on the bar TV.

He writes that he doesn't know what he got paid, because the man whose floor he slept on hadn't paid him yet.

years.cap: Moyer live as Edie Sedgwick, January 2009
years.h: We Wear White arrives under a new name
years.p: Dischord No. 175 is credited to E.D. Sedgwick, recorded mostly at Inner Ear and mixed by [[Phil Manley|726b1239-9ca1-4239-b0a0-2d64d0ec6683]]. Mother Jones ran it under "Sick of Wearing a Dress All the Time."
years.xp:
Moyer told Mother Jones he was tired of wearing a dress, and kept the name anyway: "Everyone wants to change the name of their band every time they get a new drummer. I don't really believe in that." He called it the first record he'd made with a specific group of people.

Eleven songs, from "Hex of Sex (For Minimal Man)" to "Weatherman." JosaFeen Wells joins on vocals, with Buddenhagen and Matthews as the rhythm section. Manley of [[Trans Am|7c5acaaa-3f74-4e16-82b2-f8046fce4338]] had recorded Moyer's other band [[Antelope|bad5bc3a-a2e8-41d7-95aa-b5734784fbb1]] a decade earlier.

eras.title: On hiatus, and could be back any time
eras.text: Dischord calls Edie Sedgwick an extended hiatus that could end at any moment. Moyer meanwhile made music under other names and built a second career at the Washington Post.

years.h: Moyer starts Light Beams with Arthur Noll and Sam Lavine
years.p: Light Beams is Moyer with Noll on bass and Lavine on drums. Its 2020 album Self Help won a Washington Area Music Association award, per Wikipedia.

years.h: A Pulitzer for the Washington Post, and Moyer is on the team
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Justin Moyer was part of the Post team whose January 6 coverage won a Pulitzer Prize.
